claim: Hesse (1966) gave three requirements for a good scientific analogy: material analogy (observable similarities), a causal condition on the source's vertical relations, and no essential difference in the negative analogy; she sharpened Aristotle's earlier account. SEP judges the causal and no-essential-difference conditions on the right track but too restrictive (they exclude correlational cases such as Franklin's lightning list and good analogies like rectangle/box), and rejects the narrow material-analogy requirement because formal analogies drive inference in mathematics and physics.
agent_test: Give O7 a rubric flag for the three criteria as soft flags; compare soft-flag vs no-flag at equal tokens on analogy-transfer items; also test a hard-reject variant to confirm it loses on formal analogies.
audit_note: SEP says the causal and no-essential-difference conditions are 'on the right track' but too restrictive, whereas for the material-analogy (observable similarity) requirement it says there are good reasons not to accept it in Hesse's narrow sense (formal analogies drive maths and physics).
claim_before_audit: Hesse (1966) gave three material criteria for a good scientific analogy: observable material similarity, causal (not merely correlational) vertical relations in the source, and no essential difference in the negative analogy. Aristotle already had similar criteria. SEP judges all three on the right track but too restrictive (formal analogies in maths and physics, Franklin's correlational lightning list).

claim: Bartha (2010) articulation model: classify the analogy by vertical relations in each domain; a good argument needs Prior Association (clear link in the source between shared and projected features) and Potential for Generalization (the link plausibly carries to the target, checked by listing each assumption of the source proof and its target analogue). Four vertical relation types: predictive, explanatory, functional, correlative.
agent_test: Have the agent write the source proof step list and mark each assumption as carried / not carried / unknown; code counts unknowns and caps confidence. Compare to unstructured mapping at equal tokens.

claim: There is no accepted formal logic of analogical strength. Carnapian rules, Bayesian conditionalisation and liberal Bayesianism each leave unconstrained room. Achinstein's swan/line-segment case shows a bare 'n shared properties raises probability' rule over-justifies. Norton's material theory: each inference is warranted by a local fact of analogy, not a general similarity measure.
agent_test: Do not build a numeric analogy-strength score in code; test a similarity-count scorer against a causal-link checklist on held-out analogy items and expect the count scorer to fail.
audit_note: 'Liberal Bayesianism' is not a label used verbatim in the SEP text I read; the rest (Carnapian rules, Bayesian conditionalization difficulty, Achinstein swan example, Norton warranting local fact) is present.

claim: Textbook guidelines for analogy strength (more similarity, fewer differences, less ignorance, weaker conclusion, causal over non-causal, structural over superficial) pull in different directions: Stebbing calls Reid's life-on-other-planets argument suggestive (weak conclusion), Mill rejects it (vast ignorance). Guidelines cannot be summed into a verdict.
agent_test: Ask the agent to rate several classic conflicted analogies with and without the guidelines; measure agreement with philosopher consensus. Low priority.

claim: Gentner-style systematicity is neither necessary nor sufficient for plausibility: McKay (1993) Antarctica-to-present-Mars is more systematic than Antarctica-to-ancient-Mars yet weaker, because freezing is a preventive cause. Causal direction (generative vs preventive) matters.
agent_test: Add a causal-direction field to the typed mapping in O7 and check by code that preventive relations are not mapped as generative; test on McKay-type items.

claim: Determination rules: if background knowledge says Q is fixed by P1..Pm and source and target agree on all Pi, Q transfers deductively (Davies-Russell; Weitzenfeld). Works for used-car value, fails where relevant factors are unknown (morphine/meperidine). This is the one analogy form a code check can verify fully.
agent_test: In tasks with a known determination structure, let code compare the listed determinants between source and target and block transfer if any differ; test at equal tokens vs model judgement.

claim: Keynes: once any negative analogy exists, his measure gives zero learning from positive analogy; Mill: analogy is a contest of known agreements against known differences plus vast ignorance (9 of 10 gives 0.9 only if both are random samples). Classical probability treatments are not usable as a scoring rule.
agent_test: None direct; background only.

claim: Zero-shot GPT-3 matched or beat UCLA students on standard text analogy sets: digit matrices (N=40; generative OR=1.88, p=0.005, CI 1.21-2.91; multiple choice OR=6.27, p=2.3e-8), SAT-type verbal analogies above the estimated high-school average. The result is contested: counterfactual variants break it (see K09).
agent_test: Use as the baseline claim; always pair standard and counterfactual variants when testing the agent's analogy step.

claim: Counterfactual letter-string analogies (permuted, symbol or longer-interval alphabets) break GPT models far more than humans. Lewis and Mitchell: mean accuracy over all alphabets, humans 0.753, GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452 (136 humans); extended study with 263 humans shows accuracy falling with more generalisations for all (at three generalisations humans 0.260, GPT-4 0.195, GPT-3.5 0.078). Hodel and West (121 humans) find the same for GPT-3; Stevenson et al. find children (7-9) and adults transfer to Greek and symbol alphabets while GPT-4o falls from 0.85 to 0.48 and Llama-3.1 405B to 0.27. Boundary: Webb et al. reply that GPT-4 with code execution matches humans (P=0.496).
agent_test: Test the agent on surface-changed variants of each analogy item (mutated input, G3). Allow code execution to check the mapping and compare to text-only reasoning at equal tokens.
audit_note: In Lewis and Mitchell (TMLR 2025) Table 1 the 0.078 at three generalisations belongs to GPT-3.5 (GPT-4 is 0.195, humans fall to 0.260 too, so humans also degrade with more generalisations but stay above the GPT models); all other numbers check out.
claim_before_audit: Counterfactual letter-string analogies (permuted, symbol or longer-interval alphabets) break GPT models but not humans. Lewis and Mitchell: mean accuracy over all alphabets, humans 0.753, GPT-3 0.488, GPT-3.5 0.350, GPT-4 0.452 (136 humans); extended study with 263 humans shows accuracy falling with more generalisations (GPT-4 0.078 at the hardest cell). Hodel and West (121 humans) find the same for GPT-3; Stevenson et al. find children (7-9) and adults transfer to Greek and symbol alphabets while GPT-4o falls from 0.85 to 0.48 and Llama-3.1 405B to 0.27. Boundary: Webb et al. reply that GPT-4 with code execution matches humans (P=0.496).

claim: Causal-structure story analogies: with first-order relations matched, humans choose the causally matching story (t(53)=21.3, N=54); GPT-3 is above chance in near (p=0.0039) but not far analogies (p=0.065); human vs GPT-3 OR=0.37, p=0.0003, 15/54 humans always correct. GPT-4 does better but is order-biased (WHL data 89% correct-first vs 61% correct-second; Lewis-Mitchell own run GPT-4 100% vs 72%, total 86%; humans 78% in both orders, no bias). Paraphrasing the correct story lowers GPT-4 from 0.86 to 0.72 and humans from 0.78 to 0.70 (18 problems only).
agent_test: Run the causal-match choice both ways round (answer order swapped) and require agreement in code; count order flips as a failure signal.

claim: Far (relational, cross-domain) narrative analogies are much harder for LLMs than near ones. ARN: near analogy humans 97.9 vs models 75.0; far analogy models below chance (chance 50); few-shot with chain-of-thought gets the best model only halfway between chance and humans. AnaloBench: choose the analogous story among 4 (chance 25%); GPT-4 89.1 / 66.5 / 60.7 at 1 / 10 / 30 sentences vs humans 96.0 / 72.5 / 73.3; Claude 68.2 / 30.2 / 25.9; retrieval from a bank near random. ARN Table 2 re-read: far-analogy mean humans 94.1 vs models 39.6; near 97.9 vs 75.0; overall humans 96.0 vs models 57.3; GPT-4 overall 68.1. 2026 frontier models still show a large gap on the far-analogy benchmark ARCANA (GPT 5.2 48-51% pass@3, Claude Opus 4.5 7-9%, humans 58-69% pass@1).
agent_test: Do not trust an unaided model to find a far analogue; for O7 supply or retrieve candidate analogues from a fixed bank and let code check the typed mapping. Compare retrieval-aided vs self-generated at equal tokens.
audit_note: ARCANA is a grid-transformation analogy benchmark, not narrative, and compares model pass@3 with human pass@1; numbers all match the ARN, AnaloBench and ARCANA papers.

claim: Analogical prompting (model writes its own solved examples first) beats 0-shot CoT by about +4% on average across GSM8K, MATH, Codeforces and BIG-Bench (GPT-3.5/GPT-4/PaLM2); diverse exemplars help (GSM8K 77.8 vs 75.9). The mechanism claim is contested: Qin et al. find on GSM8K and MATH (GPT-3.5) that random self-generated examples do as well or better than relevant ones (random biological about +2.5% on average over relevant math; abstract says up to 4% on GSM8K), and no-example is best on average, while relevant examples do help on BBH (+1.3% over no-example). Accuracy of the generated examples is the key factor. GAP SEARCH: Qin et al. checked accuracy directly (MATH share correct: relevant 62.0, N/A 72.0, random-same 86.0); fixed verified examples (56.3 avg) beat per-query relevant (52.4) on GPT-3.5. Relevance is not the driver on math; accuracy is.
agent_test: Run analogical prompting vs plain CoT vs random-example prompting at equal tokens on our math/puzzle set; keep O7 self-generation only if relevant beats random.

claim: Self-generated analogues need a strong base model: with text-curie-001 and davinci-001, retrieved labelled exemplars beat self-generation; the advantage appears only from davinci-002/003 up.
agent_test: Check the agent's model size is above the threshold before enabling self-generated analogues; otherwise retrieve.

claim: Inside LLMs, concept vectors for verbal relations (antonym, category) are invariant across surface forms, but abstract relations (previous/next) are not; correct internal concept can coexist with wrong output. Lee et al.: relational information is present in mid-upper layers when answers are right and missing or not propagated when wrong; patching raises accuracy.
agent_test: Not testable through a black-box scaffold; relevant as a reason why code-side mapping checks beat asking the model to introspect.

claim: Models are sensitive to irrelevant material and to semantic content: one irrelevant sentence sharply cuts GSM-IC accuracy (instruction to ignore helps, 73.5 to 79.0 on one split); content effects mirror humans (belief bias). This bears on the 'no essential difference' check: models are easily swayed by surface features. Contrary note: Qin et al. find irrelevant self-generated examples did not hurt on math.
agent_test: Test whether adding an irrelevant analogue to the prompt lowers accuracy of the O7 step; if not, drop the relevance filter.

claim: Thought Propagation: solve analogous problems, then reuse their solutions to amend the first answer; reported +12% on optimal shortest paths, +13% human preference on creative writing, +15% task completion on ALFWorld (134 tasks).
agent_test: Replicate on one planning task at equal tokens vs plain revision; stay sceptical until replicated.

claim: Generated critical questions for argument-from-analogy style schemes (Walton) are hard: no model exceeds 57% Useful zero-shot on 220 interventions rated by journalists and fact-checkers. GAP SEARCH: task-specific systems using Walton templates score about 10 points higher than the 57% zero-shot ceiling; no test on argument-from-analogy alone.
agent_test: Use Walton's critical questions as a fixed checklist written by us, not generated by the model.

claim: Raven-style matrices in text: pretrained LMs zero-shot reach above-human accuracy when features are encoded at higher abstraction (OPT 125M 22.2% to 45.6% in one comparison); moving the blank position drops GPT models but not humans (301 humans), symbol replacement changes little.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: No study found that tests an LLM on judging analogical-argument strength by Hesse's or Bartha's criteria, or implements the articulation model. This is a gap, not a negative result; searches were limited by rate limits. GAP SEARCH: arXiv title and abstract searches in Nov 2026 again found 0 papers on argument from analogy with language models.
agent_test: Build a small benchmark of 30 classic analogies (Reid, McKay, Franklin, rectangle-box) with philosopher verdicts; test model with and without a Hesse/Bartha checklist.

claim: Analogue confirmation (Dardashti et al., Hawking radiation in dumb holes) claims lab analogues can confirm predictions about inaccessible systems given an exact formal analogy; SEP calls this controversial.
agent_test: Background only.

claim: The matching step is where LLMs fail, not the generation of candidate analogies. GPT-4 given a hint found the correct source story in 15/15 runs but also accepted the wrong one (precision about 0.50-0.52, 14-15 false positives of 15); humans had precision 0.67 and recall 0.26 (n=199). This is the failure a causal-link check would target.
agent_test: Let the model propose several source analogues, then have code require a typed causal-link field and an explicit list of differences before an analogue is used; compare false-accept rate to unguided at equal tokens.

claim: Frontier 2026 models do not reliably transfer causal structure. In OpenLock transfer, only Gemini-3-Flash improved significantly (9.08 to 7.33 attempts, p=.003); GPT-5.2 got worse (-10.5%, p=.266); humans improved 33% (p<.001, N=80 reference). GPT-5.2 also treated common cause and common effect differently (11.8 vs 19.7 attempts), humans did not.
agent_test: Store causal direction (generative, preventive, common cause, common effect) as a typed field in the mapping; test transfer accuracy with and without the field on McKay-style items at equal tokens.

claim: In practice the Hesse and Bartha criteria cannot be applied as fixed code rules: SEP says Hesse gives no definition of essential beyond 'causally closely related to the known positive analogy', essentiality depends on the use of the analogy, and determination rules are rarely known (animal drug testing is the example). Hesse's own evidence is a few worked cases (heat as fluid flow failing when heat was not conserved; Franklin's lightning) plus argument, not a systematic test.
agent_test: Implement checks as soft flags with required fields (source proof steps, target analogue per step, listed differences) and measure flag precision on a hand-labelled set of classic cases (Galileo moon, heat-fluid, rectangles-boxes, life on Mars).

claim: No study tests a Hesse or Bartha checklist on LLMs at equal tokens, and no 2025-2026 reasoning-model run of the Lewis-Mitchell counterfactual letter-string variants was found. Standard letter-string items are now easy (advice correct 84.6% across four 2026 models), so the open question is variants, not the base task.
agent_test: Run the checklist vs no-checklist arms on our own labelled analogical-argument set plus a counterfactual letter-string set, same token budget.

claim: Answer-order bias in analogy choice (GPT-4 0.89 first vs 0.61 second in Webb data) is consistent with a general multiple-choice selection bias in LLMs (20 LLMs, 3 benchmarks; permutation debiasing helps). The analogy-specific evidence is still the same 18 stories, so the size on larger sets is unknown.
agent_test: Run each analogy choice in both orders in code and accept only agreeing answers; count the share of disagreements.
